story.title: Support Station Offers Comfort in Earthquake-Affected Cali
story.summary: In the aftermath of a recent earthquake in Cali, residents are finding solace at a 'hugs here' station. Led by Andres Solomon and a team of volunteers, the station provides emotional support as rescue efforts continue to clear debris from the disaster.

timeline_highlights.title: Rescue Teams Save Woman After 36 Hours Trapped in Colombia Earthquake Rubble
timeline_highlights.summary: A 32-year-old woman was rescued alive after being trapped for 36 hours under the rubble of a collapsed building in Pereira, Colombia, following a 7.4-magnitude earthquake. Rescuers located her 10 hours before successfully reaching her, as they continue to search for more survivors amid the devastation.

timeline_highlights.title: Colombia's Earthquake Rescue Operations Near Critical Conclusion
timeline_highlights.summary: Rescue operations in Colombia are entering their final phase following a magnitude 7.4 earthquake that has resulted in at least 265 fatalities and left hundreds missing. As the critical 72-hour window for finding survivors approaches its end, rescuers are intensifying their efforts in collapsed buildings across western Colombia. The earthquake has displaced tens of thousands and caused significant destruction to infrastructure.
key_facts: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia.
Death toll currently stands at 265, with hundreds missing.

event_overview.title: About Colombia Earthquake
event_overview.subject: Colombia Earthquake
event_overview.summary: The Colombia earthquake was a magnitude 7.4 earthquake that struck western Colombia on August 10, 2026, causing major building damage and trapping people beneath collapsed structures. Pereira, in the coffee-growing region of Risaralda, was among the affected cities, and the event prompted a continuing search-and-rescue and disaster-response operation.

facts.label: Start date
facts.value: The main earthquake struck on August 10, 2026; rescue and damage-assessment operations continued in the following days.

facts.label: Magnitude and affected area
facts.value: The earthquake was reported as magnitude 7.4 and affected western Colombia, including Pereira, Cali, Quibdó and Manizales; it was also felt in Ecuador and Panama.

facts.label: Pereira’s setting
facts.value: Pereira is the capital of Risaralda department and the largest city in Colombia’s Eje Cafetero (Coffee Axis); it is located in central-western Colombia.

facts.label: Seismic monitoring
facts.value: The Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC) is the national geological authority that publishes earthquake information and seismic-hazard tools; its seismic catalog contains events from 1993 onward and says entries are manually reviewed by SGC seismology analysts.

facts.label: Response framework
facts.value: Colombia’s disaster-risk system is established under Law 1523 of 2012. The law assigns disaster-risk management to national and territorial authorities and gives the National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) a coordinating role across the system.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the immediate rescue phase in Pereira on August 12-13, 2026, rather than providing a complete account of all affected places, casualty revisions, relief measures, or longer-term recovery.

related_stories.summary: Zambians voted on Thursday in a presidential election that tests the economic reforms of incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema.
